analysis:
This PR changes documentation only: docs/architecture/inference.md (a new paragraph at head lines 595-611) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (a date bump and a new DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED env-var row at head line 1741). The supplied units are the unchanged head context of inference.md (lines 1644-2222) and the cli-reference patch. The new paragraph at 595-611 is only visible in the patch excerpt, not in a numbered unit.

The docs describe a Gated DeltaNet prompt-window kernel in mlx-swift-lm. At first use per kernel instantiation it probes `packed`, then `rows`, on a fixed window. It keeps a kernel only if the output matches `gated_delta_step` bit for bit on the GPU, and otherwise falls back to the stock kernel. Decode, MTP verification, masked updates and short windows always use the stock kernel. The env var can keep the stock kernel or force `packed` or `rows` for A/B measurement.

I found no concrete security regression and no change to coordinator trust, attestation, encryption, authorization or cache scoping.

The bit-for-bit claim supports prefix-cache checkpoint integrity under T-041 and the TB-007 inference engine. The claim is unverifiable here because the kernel source is outside the supplied evidence. A forced kernel mode would bypass the probe, but it is an operator-set local environment variable. Operators are already in the ADV-001 model, where the operator can alter local behavior and outputs, so this adds no new attack surface (T-007, T-012).

The next pass should check whether GatedDelta.swift actually implements the probe and fallback as documented. It should also check that forced modes cannot silently corrupt recurrent state captured in SSD prefix-cache checkpoints. The inference.md context I did see (MiMo and Flint sections) is unchanged and not re-reviewed.
